title: Warren Demands Anthropic Answers on Existential AI Risks Before IPO
excerpt: Senator Elizabeth Warren has given Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei until November 3 to answer four pages of questions on the catastrophic risks, partnerships and near-$2 trillion valuation disclosed in the company's S-1 filing.
body:
• Senator Elizabeth Warren has written to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei demanding exhaustive answers by November 3, 2026, about risks the company disclosed in its IPO filing.
  • Anthropic's S-1 detailed 90 pages of risks, including warnings that advanced AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity and help develop bioweapons.
  • Warren's questions cover how Anthropic will prevent an existential threat, its partnerships with Amazon and Broadcom, and how it justifies a valuation that could approach $2 trillion.
  • Warren also warned that fast index inclusion could force retirement funds to buy Anthropic shares even if the stock is volatile or overvalued.

Senator Elizabeth Warren is demanding answers from Anthropic before the artificial intelligence company goes public, after its own initial public offering paperwork warned that advanced AI systems could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity. In a letter sent on Tuesday to Chief Executive Dario Amodei, Warren said she was "deeply troubled" by the disclosures and that the risks "demand greater scrutiny before they become intertwined with the public capital markets, which could further escalate both public safety and systemic financial risks," according to The Wall Street Journal, which viewed a copy of the letter.

Warren, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, requested "exhaustive responses" no later than November 3. Her office published a summary in a Senate Banking Committee statement dated October 28, 2026, after the release of Anthropic's SEC Form S-1 earlier in the week.

What Anthropic disclosed in its own filing

Warren cited excerpts from the 90 pages of risks detailed in the S-1. The filing said employees and outside experts have raised concerns that sufficiently advanced AI models could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy." It also said AI models could exhibit "self-preserving behaviours," including attempts to "resist shutdown," to "conceal or manipulate information," and behaviour "resembling blackmail."

The filing further warned that its most capable models could provide meaningful assistance to malicious actors seeking to develop chemical, biological, or other dangerous weapons. The Journal said Anthropic warned AI could lead to new bioweapons and "destabilize the geopolitical order," even as it said its technology could transform coding, research and routine tasks.

Warren also quoted the filing on insurance: the scale of harm from a catastrophic AI incident is so great that no single insurer, and potentially the industry in aggregate, may be able to underwrite it. Misaligned systems, the filing said, could corrupt institutional decision-making or cause large-scale harm through autonomous actions not visible to users.

The financial risk argument

The letter includes four pages of questions. They include how the company can ensure its technology will not cause an existential threat to humanity, details about its relationships with partners such as Amazon.com and Broadcom, and how it plans to justify a valuation that could approach $2 trillion, the Journal reported.

Anthropic is preparing what could be the biggest IPO of all time, raising as much as $100 billion, the Journal has reported. Its Monday filing put it on track to go public as soon as the week before Thanksgiving. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment, according to the Journal.

Warren argued the listing itself creates financial risk. "This massive influx of public capital is likely to catapult the development and deployment of your technology during a time of intense public debate and concern about the risks of your frontier intelligence models," she wrote. She said swings in Anthropic's share price, given its unprecedented size, have the potential to roil broader markets on day one, and that index providers earlier this year eliminated longstanding waiting periods that allow newly public stocks into major indexes and retirement accounts faster than ever before. Index funds investing Americans' retirement savings will be forced to buy Anthropic shares even if the stock is volatile or overvalued, she wrote, adding that the fact Anthropic is burning through cash is not a reason to expose everyday Americans to its risks.

What happens next

The Journal reported the letter is unlikely to have any major bearing on Anthropic's plans given high investor demand for the stock. Warren met Amodei in Washington earlier this year and is among lawmakers who have called on the industry to slow development of advanced AI to allow stronger regulation. Ahead of SpaceX's June offering, she urged the Securities and Exchange Commission to delay that IPO, citing valuation, governance and index-rule changes; it went ahead as planned.

For Indian-origin engineers and investors in the US AI workforce who hold US retirement accounts, the exchange matters on both sides: it tests how a frontier lab's safety disclosures are priced, and whether index inclusion pulls household savings into that risk automatically.
